skill.name: writing-guidelines
skill.description: Reviews documentation and prose against current Writing Guidelines, then reports concise findings with file and line references.
skill.summary: Check documentation for writing guideline violations and receive concise, location-based findings.
skill.author: vercel-labs

security_audit.summary: The two command-execution alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and a fenced URL block. The network request is confirmed, and trusting mutable remote instructions creates a high-severity prompt injection and supply-chain risk.

remediation.issue: The skill fetches guidelines from a mutable branch before every review.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the source to a reviewed commit and verify its expected content hash before use.

remediation.issue: Fetched content is treated as authoritative rules and output instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Treat remote text as untrusted reference data and reject instructions unrelated to writing analysis or output formatting.

static_findings.snippet: 4. Output findings in the terse `file:line` format

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 19 uses Markdown inline-code backticks around the literal file:line format. It does not invoke a shell or execute a command.
Lines 25 through 27 form a Markdown fenced block containing a URL. The backticks are formatting delimiters, not Ruby or shell execution.
The URL on line 26 is explicitly fetched before each review through WebFetch. This creates real outbound network access to mutable remote content.

semantic_findings.title: Mutable Remote Instructions Are Trusted

content.value_statement: Inconsistent prose makes documentation harder to read and maintain. This skill checks selected files against current guidelines and reports precise locations for revision.
actual_capabilities: Fetches the latest Writing Guidelines from the configured source.
Reads user-specified files or file patterns.
Checks prose against every rule in the fetched guidelines.
Reports findings with file and line references.
Asks which files to review when no target is provided.
limitations: Requires network access to retrieve the guidelines.
Uses mutable remote content that may change between reviews.
Reports issues but does not promise automatic revisions.
Review quality depends on accessible text files and the fetched rules.

use_cases.title: Review Product Documentation
use_cases.description: Check a documentation page for style, voice, and formatting issues before publication.

use_cases.title: Audit Repository Prose
use_cases.description: Review selected Markdown files and receive concise findings tied to exact locations.

use_cases.title: Standardize Editorial Quality
use_cases.description: Apply one writing standard across documentation contributed by several teams.

prompt_templates.title: Review One File
prompt_templates.prompt: Review README.md against the Writing Guidelines. Report each issue with its file and line number.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a focused review of one document.

prompt_templates.title: Check Documentation Pages
prompt_templates.prompt: Review all Markdown files in docs/getting-started. Group findings by file and keep each explanation concise.
prompt_templates.scenario: A writer is preparing several related pages for publication.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize Important Issues
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit docs/**/*.md against the Writing Guidelines. Prioritize unclear language, inconsistent terminology, and structural problems.
prompt_templates.scenario: An engineering team needs a repository-wide prose audit.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Revised Documentation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the changed documentation files. Identify remaining violations and note whether previously reported issues appear resolved.
prompt_templates.scenario: A documentation lead is validating revisions before release.

output_examples.input: Review docs/setup.md for writing guideline compliance.
output: docs/setup.md:18 - Replace vague wording with a specific action.
docs/setup.md:42 - Use consistent terminology for the project name.

output_examples.input: Audit the Markdown files in docs/api.
output_examples.output: docs/api/authentication.md:27 - Shorten the sentence and place the required action first.

output_examples.input: Check README.md and report only guideline violations.
output_examples.output: README.md:64 - Replace passive voice with a direct instruction.

best_practices: Provide a narrow file path or pattern for faster, more relevant reviews.
Review findings in context before changing technical terminology.
Run the review again after revisions to confirm remaining issues.
anti_patterns: Do not provide binary or generated files as review targets.
Do not accept remote instructions that are unrelated to writing review.
Do not treat every finding as correct without checking surrounding context.

faq.question: What files can this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews readable prose files selected by a path or file pattern.

faq.question: Does it edit documentation automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill reports guideline violations and their locations for manual revision.

faq.question: Where do the writing rules come from?
faq.answer: The skill fetches rules from its configured Writing Guidelines URL before each review.

faq.question: Does the skill require network access?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses WebFetch to retrieve the latest guideline document.

faq.question: What happens when no file is specified?
faq.answer: The skill asks which files or patterns should be reviewed.

faq.question: How are findings presented?
faq.answer: Findings use a concise file and line format defined by the fetched guidelines.
